dataset: Indiana University Chest X-Ray Collection (Open-i / NLM)

Atelectasis.clinical_notes: Frequently observed at lung bases or as linear/bandlike opacities. Highly represented in IU X-Ray reports.

Consolidation.clinical_notes: Very frequently negated in normal/unremarkable studies ('no focal consolidation').

Infiltration.clinical_notes: Older radiological descriptor often replaced by 'airspace opacity', 'consolidation', or 'interstitial markings'. Frequently negated ('clear of focal infiltrate').

Pneumothorax.clinical_notes: Critical acute condition. Most commonly mentioned as an explicit negative ('no evidence of pneumothorax') in 57.5% of all reports.

Edema.clinical_notes: Often paired with heart failure or vascular congestion assessments in elderly cohorts.

Emphysema.clinical_notes: Commonly described via secondary visual signs like hyperinflated lungs or flattened hemidiaphragms.

Fibrosis.clinical_notes: In reports, often described as 'prominent interstitial markings' or 'apical scarring/fibrotic changes'.

Effusion.clinical_notes: One of the top findings in the entire dataset. 688 positive cases, and 1,916 negated occurrences ('no pleural effusion').

Pneumonia.clinical_notes: Pneumonia is a clinical diagnosis; radiologists usually describe visual correlates ('focal consolidation', 'airspace opacity') and mention pneumonia in IMPRESSION as a differential.

Pleural_Thickening.clinical_notes: Less frequent in isolation; frequently noted at the apices ('apical capping/scarring').

Cardiomegaly.clinical_notes: High positive representation. Also routinely noted as normal ('heart size within normal limits').

Nodule.clinical_notes: Very high occurrence in IU X-Ray, predominantly due to benign calcified granulomas from endemic fungal exposure (histoplasmosis).

Mass.clinical_notes: Used for lesions > 3 cm or ill-defined bulky opacities. Frequently followed by recommendation for chest CT.

Hernia.clinical_notes: Almost exclusively refers to hiatal hernia presenting as retrocardiac soft tissue mass with or without air.

Lung Lesion.clinical_notes: Rare generic term; clinical radiologists prefer specific descriptors ('nodule', 'mass', 'granuloma', 'opacity').

Fracture.clinical_notes: Commonly relates to rib fractures or osteoporotic spine compression fractures.

Lung Opacity.clinical_notes: The most frequent radiological descriptor in the entire dataset (835 positive instances). Broad superset covering consolidation, atelectasis, and scarring.

Enlarged Cardiomediastinum.clinical_notes: The exact phrase is rare in IU X-Ray; reports routinely differentiate between cardiomegaly and tortuous aorta or mediastinal contour.

non_model_frequent_report_concepts.description: Explicit confirmation of normal pulmonary parenchyma, clear costophrenic angles, and normal cardiomediastinal contour.
Thoracic spondylosis, scoliosis, osteophytes, and degenerative disc disease.
Benign calcified granulomas (often histoplasmosis) and vascular calcification.
Sternotomy wires, surgical clips, pacemakers, leads, and central venous catheters.
Tortuous ectatic thoracic aorta, aortic arch calcification.
